title: Landmine Squat
summary: A squat holding the end of a landmine bar at your chest, which lets you sit upright and deep with little load on the spine.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: landmine attachment; barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.6 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.5 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.2 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.
Library rating 0.1 for upper back: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly upper back total.

setup.text: Hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands and step back so you lean slightly into it.
Sit straight down between your hips, keeping your chest up.
Go as deep as you can control, then drive up through your mid-foot.

form_cues.cue: Keep the bar at your chest
Lean into the bar a little. It acts like a counterweight and helps you stay upright.

mistakes.text: Letting the bar drift away from your chest.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stable, One side at a time, Less systemic fatigue.
